# Node reference

Every node type in the registry (58 types, definition version 1), grouped by role. Node ids in a document are free-form; the **type** is what you pick. Set parameters with the MCP tools (see mcp-tools.md) using the parameter **id** and a value of the listed type and range.

How to read the tables:
- **Ports** carry typed connections: an output connects only to an input of the same port type (and unit). `connections: many` inputs accept several links (they are ordered); `one` accepts a single link. Outputs always fan out: one output (a particle chain, an event, a path set) can feed any number of inputs, e.g. the same Emitter particles into a renderer and into ParticleEvents. `required: yes` inputs must be connected or compile reports an error.
- **Unit** values: meter, second, tick (60 per second), radian, metersPerSecond, metersPerSecondSquared, hertz, perSecond, linearGain, normalized (0..1), none. A connection must match the unit exactly (use ScalarMath/Constant with a Unit to convert).
- **default** shows curves and gradients compactly (`curve normalized/linear: 0:1 1:0`, `gradient: 0:#FFFFFF 1:#FF8000`). The JSON you pass to vfx_set_params / vfx_add_node is: curve `{ "domain": "normalized", "interpolation": "linear", "keys": [{ "x": 0, "y": 1 }, { "x": 1, "y": 0 }] }` (2-16 keys, x ascending); gradient `{ "stops": [{ "position": 0, "color": { "srgb": "#FFFFFF", "alpha": 1 } }, { "position": 1, "color": { "srgb": "#FF8000", "alpha": 0 } }] }` (2-8 stops). Colours everywhere are `{ "srgb": "#RRGGBB", "alpha": 1 }`. `vfx_describe_node_type` shows the exact default JSON.
- **range** is the accepted min..max (values outside are rejected, never clamped). Vector parameters list one bound for every component.
- **drive**: number, integer, boolean, colour, vec2, vec3 and quaternion parameters are also implicit input ports named after the parameter; connect a signal node (Constant, RandomRange, ScalarMath, Oscillator, Time, EffectTimeCurve, PublicParameter) whose output unit and evaluation domain match. `domains` lists which signal domains the parameter accepts (constant = fixed; effectTime = varies over effect time; normalizedAge = varies over particle life; pathU = varies along a path). Integer parameters accept only constant sources. Curve/gradient parameters take a Curve/Gradient node (curveValue/gradientValue). Enum and string parameters cannot be driven.
- **edit**: live = a change applies instantly while playing; resample = the effect is re-simulated after a change (still fast, but not per-frame).
- **Disabled behaviour**: what a disabled node does (empty = nothing, bypass = passes its input through, fallback = consumers use their literal).
- **Portability**: core (exports faithfully), approximation (exports approximately), enhancement (preview only) relative to the Roblox export.
- Defaults are the values a freshly created node gets when a parameter is not given.

## Sources, timing and events

Where and when things happen: anchors (positions), schedules (windows/cues) and event plumbing.

### Anchor

A position in the effect: the document anchor "source", "target" or a custom anchor id. Wire `out` into any anchor input (emitters, renderers, paths, lights). The document anchors themselves are moved with the anchor tools, not with this node.

- Category: Sources, timing and events; portability: core; disabled = consumers use their own literal; definition version 1.

**Inputs**

None declared. (Number/boolean/colour/vector parameters can still be driven, see the Drive column.)

**Outputs** (each output can feed any number of inputs)

| id | label | type | domains |
|---|---|---|---|
| `out` | Anchor | anchor | — |

**Parameters**

| id | label | type | unit | default | range | choices | edit | domains | drive | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `anchorId` | Anchor | string | — | `source` | — | — | resample | constant | — | Document anchor ID (source, target or a custom anchor). |

### Schedule

Timing gate. Outputs a timeWindow (needed by continuous emitters, sprites, lights, ribbons) and start/end events (feed Emitter.trigger for bursts). Modes: once (one cue at Start), window (open from Start for Duration), repeat (repeats every Repeat interval, Repeat count times). The optional trigger input starts the schedule relative to an event (Start becomes a delay after that event). All times are ticks, 60 per second.

- Category: Sources, timing and events; portability: core; disabled = produces nothing; definition version 1.

**Inputs**

| id | label | type | connections | required | domains |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trigger` | Trigger | event | one | no | — |

**Outputs** (each output can feed any number of inputs)

| id | label | type | domains |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | Start | event | — |
| `end` | End | event | — |
| `window` | Window | timeWindow | — |

**Parameters**

| id | label | type | unit | default | range | choices | edit | domains | drive | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `startTicks` | Start | integer | tick | `0` | 0..600 step 1 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | When the cue/window starts, in ticks from effect start (or delay after the trigger event when one is connected). |
| `durationTicks` | Duration | integer | tick | `60` | 1..600 step 1 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | How long the window stays open (window/repeat modes), in ticks. |
| `mode` | Mode | enum | — | `once` | — | once, window, repeat | resample | constant | — | once = single cue at Start; window = open from Start for Duration; repeat = repeats every Repeat interval, Repeat count times. |
| `repeatIntervalTicks` | Repeat interval | integer | tick | `60` | 1..600 step 1 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Used only in repeat mode. |
| `repeatCount` | Repeat count | integer | — | `1` | 1..128 step 1 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Used only in repeat mode. |

### OffsetAnchor

An anchor moved by a fixed offset from another anchor (a floor point under the Target, a point above a hand). With dropToGround it is projected onto the ground. Prefer it to a separate fixed document anchor for anything that must follow Target.

- Category: Sources, timing and events; portability: core; disabled = passes its input straight through (anchor -> out); definition version 1.

**Inputs**

| id | label | type | connections | required | domains |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `anchor` | Anchor | anchor | one | yes | — |

**Outputs** (each output can feed any number of inputs)

| id | label | type | domains |
|---|---|---|---|
| `out` | Out | anchor | — |

**Parameters**

| id | label | type | unit | default | range | choices | edit | domains | drive | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `offset` | Offset | vec3 | meter | `[0, 1, 0]` | -100..100 | — | resample | constant | vec3Signal | Offset from the source anchor (m), as x,y,z (y = up). |
| `dropToGround` | Drop to ground | boolean | — | `false` | — | — | resample | constant | booleanSignal | Follow the anchor sideways but sit on the ground (height = Offset Y). For ground rings, scorch marks and light pools under a moving Target. |

## Emitters

Create particles.

### Emitter

Creates particles. Continuous emission = Rate + a connected window with Burst 0. Bursts = Burst + a connected trigger event (Schedule start, PathFollower arrival, ParticleEvents...). Position comes from an anchor (or from paths with shape "path"); Aim overrides Direction. Lifetimes are seconds; speeds metres per second. Its `particles` output starts a particle chain.

- Category: Emitters; portability: core; disabled = produces nothing; definition version 1.

**Inputs**

| id | label | type | connections | required | domains |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `anchor` | Anchor | anchor | one | no | — |
| `paths` | Paths | paths | one | no | — |
| `trigger` | Trigger | event | many | no | — |
| `window` | Window | timeWindow | one | no | — |
| `aim` | Aim | anchor | one | no | — |

**Outputs** (each output can feed any number of inputs)

| id | label | type | domains |
|---|---|---|---|
| `particles` | Particles | particles | — |

**Parameters**

| id | label | type | unit | default | range | choices | edit | domains | drive | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `shape` | Shape | enum | — | `point` | — | point, cone, sphere, disc, box, path | resample | constant | — | Where particles spawn: point, cone, sphere, disc, box, or along the paths of a connected path set ("path"). |
| `burst` | Burst | integer | — | `32` | 0..4096 step 1 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Particles per trigger event (needs the Trigger input). For continuous emission only, set Burst to 0 and use Rate with a Window. |
| `rate` | Rate | number | perSecond | `0` | 0..4096 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Continuous particles per second while the window is open. |
| `rateOverWindow` | Rate over window | curve | — | `curve normalized/linear: 0:1 1:1` | 0..4 (normalized curve) | — | resample | constant | curveValue | Rate multiplier across the emission window (0 = window start, 1 = end): ramps, pulses, tails. |
| `lifetimeMin` | Lifetime min | number | second | `0.6` | 0.0166667..10 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Authored in seconds; simulation converts to ticks. |
| `lifetimeMax` | Lifetime max | number | second | `1.2` | 0.0166667..10 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Authored in seconds; simulation converts to ticks. |
| `radius` | Radius | number | meter | `0.2` | 0..20 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Size of the spawn shape (m): cone/sphere/disc radius, box half-extent. |
| `coneAngle` | Cone angle | number | radian | `0.349066` | 0..3.14159 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Cone shape: half-angle of the spread around the emit axis (the Aim direction when Aim is connected, else Direction). 0 = a straight line, π/2 = a hemisphere. Particles start on a disc of Radius across the axis. |
| `speedMin` | Speed min | number | metersPerSecond | `1` | 0..100 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Lowest initial speed (m/s); each particle picks a random speed between min and max. |
| `speedMax` | Speed max | number | metersPerSecond | `3` | 0..100 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Highest initial speed (m/s). Must be >= Speed min. |
| `direction` | Direction | vec3 | — | `[1, 0, 0]` | -1..1 | — | resample | constant | vec3Signal | Spread direction (local +X axis); normalized at compile time. Ignored when the Aim input is connected. |
| `space` | Space | enum | — | `world` | — | world, local | resample | constant | — | world only for now (local is reserved); the emit axis always follows Aim/Direction. |
| `useEventPosition` | Use event position | boolean | — | `true` | — | — | resample | constant | booleanSignal | When triggered by an event that has a position (ParticleEvents, collision), spawn there instead of at the anchor. |
| `inheritVelocity` | Inherit velocity | number | normalized | `0` | 0..1 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Particle-event triggers only: fraction of the parent particle velocity added to each child (e.g. debris carried along by a moving spark). |

## Particle operators

Sit in a particle chain (Emitter -> ... -> renderer) and change the particles: initial look, forces, life curves, events.

### InitialProperties

Sets each new particle's size, starting rotation, spin and colour (random between the min/max pair) and whether flipbooks start on a random frame. Modifier: bypassed when disabled.

- Category: Particle operators; portability: core; disabled = passes its input straight through (particles -> particles); definition version 1.

**Inputs**

| id | label | type | connections | required | domains |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `particles` | Particles | particles | one | yes | — |

**Outputs** (each output can feed any number of inputs)

| id | label | type | domains |
|---|---|---|---|
| `particles` | Particles | particles | — |

**Parameters**

| id | label | type | unit | default | range | choices | edit | domains | drive | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sizeMin` | Size min | number | meter | `0.08` | 0.001..20 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Smallest starting particle size (m); random between min and max. |
| `sizeMax` | Size max | number | meter | `0.16` | 0.001..20 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Largest starting particle size (m). |
| `rotationMin` | Rotation min | number | radian | `0` | -6.28319..6.28319 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Lowest starting rotation (radians, -2pi..2pi); random between min and max. |
| `rotationMax` | Rotation max | number | radian | `6.28319` | -6.28319..6.28319 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Highest starting rotation (radians). |
| `angularVelocityMin` | Angular velocity min | number | perSecond | `-20` | -20..20 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Radians per second. |
| `angularVelocityMax` | Angular velocity max | number | perSecond | `20` | -20..20 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Radians per second. |
| `color` | Color | color | — | `#FFFFFF` | — | — | resample | constant | colorSignal | Starting particle colour (multiplied with the Material tint and colour over life). |
| `randomFrameStart` | Random frame start | boolean | — | `false` | — | — | resample | constant | booleanSignal | Flipbook particles start on a random frame so they do not animate in lockstep. |

### Gravity

Constant world-space acceleration (negative Y falls, positive Y rises like smoke or flame). Strength scales it 0..1 and can be animated.

- Category: Particle operators; portability: core; disabled = passes its input straight through (particles -> particles); definition version 1.

**Inputs**

| id | label | type | connections | required | domains |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `particles` | Particles | particles | one | yes | — |

**Outputs** (each output can feed any number of inputs)

| id | label | type | domains |
|---|---|---|---|
| `particles` | Particles | particles | — |

**Parameters**

| id | label | type | unit | default | range | choices | edit | domains | drive | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `strength` | Strength | number | normalized | `1` | 0..1 | — | live | constant/effectTime | scalarSignal | Gain on this force (0..1); drive with an EffectTimeCurve to ramp it over time. |
| `acceleration` | Acceleration | vec3 | metersPerSecondSquared | `[0, -9.81, 0]` | -100..100 | — | resample | constant | vec3Signal | World-space acceleration in m/s². Positive Y gives buoyancy (rising smoke/flame). |

### Drag

Exponential velocity damping. Smoke, embers and event-born particles that inherit speed nearly always need some Drag.

- Category: Particle operators; portability: core; disabled = passes its input straight through (particles -> particles); definition version 1.

**Parameters**

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `strength` | Strength | number | normalized | `1` | 0..1 | — | live | constant/effectTime | scalarSignal | Gain on this force (0..1); drive with an EffectTimeCurve to ramp it over time. |
| `coefficient` | Coefficient | number | perSecond | `0.8` | 0..20 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Exponential velocity damping: velocity *= exp(-coefficient·dt). |

- Category: Particle operators; portability: approximation; disabled = passes its input straight through (particles -> particles); definition version 1.

| `restitution` | Restitution | number | normalized | `0.2` | 0..1 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Fraction of vertical speed kept on each bounce. |

## Paths

Curves in space (beams, bolts, rings, projectile routes): generators, modifiers and the follower.

### PathFollower

Moves along every path of its set at once: the `anchor` output follows each path (carry a glowing core, emitters, lights, trails on it) and everything attached is repeated per path (5 paths = 5 projectiles, each emitting the full rate). The `arrival` event fires once per path when it gets there (trigger impact bursts so each impact lands exactly on time; a Schedule started by the arrival starts at the first one). Give Travel ticks or a Speed (speed mode: each path takes its own length / speed). Use PathSplitter in front of it to choose which paths.

- Category: Paths; portability: core; disabled = produces nothing; definition version 1.

**Inputs**

| id | label | type | connections | required | domains |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `paths` | Paths | paths | one | yes | — |
| `window` | Window | timeWindow | one | yes | — |

**Outputs** (each output can feed any number of inputs)

| id | label | type | domains |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anchor` | Anchor | anchor | — |
| `arrival` | Arrival | event | — |

**Parameters**

| id | label | type | unit | default | range | choices | edit | domains | drive | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `durationTicks` | Travel ticks | integer | tick | `30` | 1..600 step 1 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Ticks every path of the set takes from start to end; arrival fires then. Holds at the end until the window closes. |
| `easing` | Easing | enum | — | `linear` | — | linear, easeIn, easeOut, easeInOut | resample | constant | — | Speed profile of the travel: linear, easeIn (slow start), easeOut (slow end), easeInOut. |
| `speed` | Speed | number | metersPerSecond | `0` | 0..200 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | 0 = travel for Travel ticks. Above 0: travel ticks = path length ÷ speed (rounded to ticks, per path), so a farther Target, or a longer path, takes longer at the same speed. |

### PathSplitter

Decides which paths of a set go on and which are left behind. `paths` = the chosen ones (kept in their original order), `rest` = all the others. Modes: range (a few in a row), everyNth (every other one...), random (a fixed random pick), longest / shortest. Works anywhere paths flow: into a PathFollower (only the chosen ones fly), a renderer, or a modifier.

- Category: Paths; portability: core; disabled = passes its input straight through (paths -> paths); definition version 1.

**Inputs**

| id | label | type | connections | required | domains |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `paths` | Paths | paths | one | yes | — |

**Outputs** (each output can feed any number of inputs)

| id | label | type | domains |
|---|---|---|---|
| `paths` | Chosen | paths | — |
| `rest` | Rest | paths | — |

**Parameters**

| id | label | type | unit | default | range | choices | edit | domains | drive | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | Mode | enum | — | `range` | — | range, everyNth, random, longest, shortest | resample | constant | — | range: Count paths starting at From. everyNth: every Step-th path starting at Offset. random: Count paths picked at random (same pick every time; change the random stream of the node or the document seed for another pick). longest / shortest: the Count longest / shortest paths. |
| `from` | From | integer | — | `0` | 0..255 step 1 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | range mode: index of the first chosen path (0 = the first path). |
| `count` | Count | integer | — | `1` | 1..256 step 1 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | range, random, longest and shortest modes: how many paths go on. |
| `step` | Step | integer | — | `2` | 1..256 step 1 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | everyNth mode: take every Step-th path (2 = every other one). |
| `offset` | Offset | integer | — | `0` | 0..255 step 1 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | everyNth mode: index of the first chosen path. |

## Renderers and lights

Turn particles, paths and anchors into visible output. Each needs a Material (except PointLight) and an output connection to EffectOutput.visual.

### RingRenderer

A closed ring at an anchor whose radius follows a curve over its window (shockwaves). Simpler than RingPath + RibbonRenderer.

- Category: Renderers and lights; portability: core; disabled = produces nothing; definition version 1.

**Inputs**

| id | label | type | connections | required | domains |

| `material` | Material | material | one | yes | — |
| `window` | Window | timeWindow | one | no | — |

| id | label | type | domains |

| `visual` | Visual | visual | — |

| id | label | type | unit | default | range | choices | edit | domains | drive | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `width` | Width | number | meter | `0.03` | 0.001..5 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Ring strip width (m). |

## Materials

How a renderer is shaded (colour, blend, texture, lighting).

### Material

Shading for a renderer: template (SpriteUnlit, SpriteTextured, RibbonUnlit, MeshLit, SurfaceTranslucent, DarkVolumeSprite), blend (additive or normal), tint, opacity, emission, texture/sprite, dissolve, lighting, hueShift and recolour. One Material can feed several renderers.

- Category: Materials; portability: core; disabled = consumers use their own literal; definition version 1.

**Inputs**

None declared. (Number/boolean/colour/vector parameters can still be driven, see the Drive column.)

**Outputs** (each output can feed any number of inputs)

| id | label | type | domains |
|---|---|---|---|
| `material` | Material | material | — |

**Parameters**

| id | label | type | unit | default | range | choices | edit | domains | drive | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `template` | Template | enum | — | `SpriteUnlit` | — | SpriteUnlit, SpriteTextured, RibbonUnlit, MeshLit, SurfaceTranslucent, DarkVolumeSprite | resample | constant | — | SpriteUnlit: soft disc. SpriteTextured: a library/imported sprite or flipbook. RibbonUnlit: plain strips. MeshLit: lit PBR meshes. SurfaceTranslucent: water/ice-like (normal blend, liquid shading, reflection, optional refraction). DarkVolumeSprite: dark textured smoke (no emission; edge tint = rim colour). |
| `textureAsset` | Texture asset | string | — | `""` | — | — | resample | constant | — | Imported texture/flipbook asset ID (Import texture…); when set it replaces Sprite. Empty = use the included library sprite. |
| `normalAsset` | Normal map | string | — | `""` | — | — | resample | constant | — | Lit meshes: an imported texture with role Normal adds fine surface relief (tangent-space, uses the mesh UVs). Empty = none. |
| `noiseAsset` | Noise texture | string | — | `""` | — | — | resample | constant | — | An imported texture with role Noise replaces the included dissolve noise (billboard dissolve pattern). Empty = included noise. |
| `sprite` | Sprite | enum | — | `soft-glow` | — | flame-tongue-a, flame-tongue-b, fire-puff, smoke-puff, foam, soft-glow, spark-streak, electric-arc, droplet, bubble, ripple-ring, dissolve-noise, lightning-charge, wisp, dark-wisp, star-ray, gradient | resample | constant | — | Included library sheet (SpriteTextured only). Flipbooks animate; variant sets pick one cell per particle. |
| `variant` | Variant | integer | — | `-1` | -1..255 step 1 | — | resample | constant | scalarSignal | Variant/mask sheets: -1 picks a random cell per particle; otherwise this fixed cell (row-major). |
| `blend` | Blend | enum | — | `additive` | — | normal, additive, cutout | resample | constant | — | additive = adds light (fire, glow, sparks); normal = alpha blending (smoke, dark stuff); cutout = hard-edged alpha test. |
| `tint` | Tint | color | — | `#FFFFFF` | — | — | live | constant/effectTime/normalizedAge | colorSignal | Colour multiplied into the sprite/mesh (grey-scale sprites take their colour from here). |
| `opacity` | Opacity | number | normalized | `1` | 0..1 | — | live | constant/effectTime/normalizedAge | scalarSignal | Overall opacity multiplier 0..1. |
| `emission` | Emission | number | linearGain | `0` | 0..20 | — | live | constant/effectTime/normalizedAge | scalarSignal | Extra self-illumination / brightness multiplier (feeds bloom). 0 = none; above 1 over-brightens. |
| `uvScroll` | UV scroll | vec2 | — | `[0, 0]` | -10..10 | — | live | constant | vec2Signal | Texture flow in UV units per second of effect time (x along a ribbon, y across). Textured ribbons and textured billboards. |
| `uvTiling` | UV tiling | vec2 | — | `[1, 1]` | 0.01..32 | — | live | constant | vec2Signal | Texture repeats per sprite (09). Textured billboards. |
| `uvOffset` | UV offset | vec2 | — | `[0, 0]` | -1..1 | — | live | constant | vec2Signal | Texture shift in UV units. Textured billboards. |
| `uvRotation` | UV rotation | number | radian | `0` | -6.2832..6.2832 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Texture rotation about the sprite centre (radians). Textured billboards. |
| `uvDistort` | UV distortion | number | normalized | `0` | 0..0.15 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Noise wobble of the texture lookup (09: 0–.15 normalized UV). Textured ribbons. |
| `roughness` | Roughness | number | normalized | `0.75` | 0.04..1 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Lit meshes: low = glossy facets (ice ≈ .18). |
| `metalness` | Metalness | number | normalized | `0.05` | 0..1 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Lit meshes only. |
| `reflection` | Reflection | number | normalized | `0` | 0..3 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Lit meshes: mirrors a soft studio sky, so glossy surfaces (low Roughness) shine. Ice about 1.2, wet stone about .4, 0 = off. |
| `surfaceDetail` | Surface detail | number | normalized | `0` | 0..1 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Lit meshes: procedural bumps, grain and patchy roughness on the surface. Stone about .7, ice about .3, 0 = smooth. |
| `detailScale` | Detail scale | number | — | `4` | 0.5..30 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Size of the surface detail: higher = finer grain. |
| `recolorFrom` | Recolour from | color | — | `#808080@0` | — | — | live | constant | colorSignal | Per-part colour: the material representative colour, mapped onto Recolour to (hue, saturation and brightness). Alpha 0 = off. |
| `recolorTo` | Recolour to | color | — | `#808080@0` | — | — | live | constant | colorSignal | Per-part colour: what Recolour from becomes; every other colour of the material moves the same way. |
| `hueShift` | Colour shift | number | — | `0` | -180..180 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Rotates every colour this material draws (tint, colour over life and the colours baked into the texture) around the colour wheel: 180 turns orange fire blue, 120 green. Brightness is kept. 0 = unchanged. (degrees) |
| `liquid` | Liquid | number | normalized | `0` | 0..1 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Ribbons: a clear liquid look. The middle turns see-through, the edges catch light and highlights run along the flow. Use a pale Tint with Blend normal. Water about .85, 0 = solid colour. |
| `colorVariation` | Colour variation | number | normalized | `0` | 0..1 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Meshes: every piece gets a slightly different shade and hue (natural stone, crystal clusters). 0 = all identical. |
| `rim` | Rim glow | number | linearGain | `0` | 0..8 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Meshes: glow on edges seen side-on (fresnel), e.g. energy shells or backlit ice. Billboards: a radial glow toward the sprite edge (a flat sprite has no useful normal). 0 = off. |
| `rimColor` | Rim colour | color | — | `#FFFFFF` | — | — | live | constant | colorSignal | Edge (fresnel) glow colour for lit meshes. |
| `rimPower` | Rim sharpness | number | — | `3` | 0.5..8 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Higher = thinner rim hugging the silhouette. |
| `dissolve` | Dissolve | number | normalized | `0` | 0..1 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | How far each particle burns away through a noise pattern by the end of its life (09 dissolve; 1 = fully gone). 0 = off. Billboards only. |
| `dissolveStart` | Dissolve start | number | normalized | `0.3` | 0..0.95 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Fraction of the particle life before dissolving begins. |
| `dissolveSoftness` | Dissolve softness | number | normalized | `0.08` | 0.001..0.5 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Width of the soft edge of the dissolve/erosion transition (normalized). |
| `dissolveEdge` | Dissolve edge width | number | normalized | `0` | 0..0.25 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Width of a glowing band on the burning edge (0 = none). |
| `dissolveEdgeColor` | Dissolve edge colour | color | — | `#FFB040` | — | — | live | constant | colorSignal | Colour of the burning edge while dissolving. |
| `groundFade` | Ground fade | number | meter | `0` | 0..2 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Sprites fade out over this height above the floor (y = 0) instead of being cut by it (08 analytic ground fade). 0 = off. |
| `faceMode` | Faces | enum | — | `front` | — | front, back, double | live | constant | — | Meshes: which faces are drawn (double for thin open shapes). Camera-facing sprites and ribbons always face the camera. |
| `depthTest` | Depth test | boolean | — | `true` | — | — | live | constant | booleanSignal | Off: always drawn on top of solid objects (UI-like glows). |
| `refraction` | Refraction | number | — | `0` | 0..8 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Enhancement: bends what is behind (pixels at 1080p). Previewed on lit meshes (ice, glass); sprites and ribbons show a notice instead. |
| `alphaCutoff` | Alpha cutoff | number | normalized | `0.5` | 0..1 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Cutout blend only. |

## Output and groups

The effect output and the structural nodes that nest graphs (components inserted as groups use these).

### EffectOutput

The single output of the effect: connect renderers to `visual` (and audio/presentation). Also holds the glow (bloom) settings for the whole effect. It cannot be disabled.

- Category: Output and groups; portability: core; cannot be disabled; definition version 1.

**Inputs**

| id | label | type | connections | required | domains |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `visual` | Visual | visual | many | no | — |
| `audio` | Audio | audio | many | no | — |
| `presentation` | Presentation | presentation | many | no | — |

**Outputs** (each output can feed any number of inputs)

None.

**Parameters**

| id | label | type | unit | default | range | choices | edit | domains | drive | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `glowStrength` | Glow strength | number | — | `0.8` | 0..3 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | How strong the bloom halo around bright parts is (0 = no glow). |
| `glowRadius` | Glow radius | number | normalized | `0.45` | 0..1 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | How far the halo spreads (lower = tighter glow hugging the shapes). |
| `glowThreshold` | Glow threshold | number | — | `1` | 0..8 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Brightness above which things glow. |
| `glowLimit` | Glow limit | number | — | `3` | 0..50 | — | live | constant | scalarSignal | Caps how bright any spot counts for the glow, so many overlapping additive sprites do not flood the frame with a halo (0 = no cap; lower = tighter). |

### Group

Embeds another graph as one node (a component inserted as a group). Its ports come from the embedded graph's interface; knobs are the group's exposed controls.

- Category: Output and groups; portability: core; disabled = produces nothing; definition version 1.

**Inputs**

None declared. (Number/boolean/colour/vector parameters can still be driven, see the Drive column.)

**Outputs** (each output can feed any number of inputs)

None.

**Parameters**

| id | label | type | unit | default | range | choices | edit | domains | drive | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `graphId` | Graph | string | — | `""` | — | — | resample | constant | — | Structural embedded-graph reference; not bindable or connectable. |
